primary_topics: Marker-laying ceremony for the permanent Court of Appeals (CA) Cebu building, November 24, 2006 -- twelve days before CJP's mandatory retirement

The CA Cebu building history: Administrative Circular 61-2004 (CJ Davide, December 4, 2004); P40M from the Judiciary Development Fund; increased to P70M December 2005; Cebu provincial government donated the 2,000 sqm site

The Cebu historical parallel: April 14, 1521 -- Cebu received Christianity (King Humabon and Queen Juana baptized); 2006 -- Cebu facilitates access to justice. 'In 1521, Cebu helped spread the faith; in 2006, it facilitated access to justice.'
Values: ACID problems addressed by greater access through the new CA building; DHL for 26,000 court employees; four Ins for the nine CA Cebu justices
sub_topics: Opening: 'Maayong hapon kaninyong tanan.' -- Cebuano greeting; CJP acknowledges the Queen City of the South for its 'hospitality and warmth and the angelic voices of its people'

Building history: dream started in 2004; December 4, 2004 -- CJ Davide issued Administrative Circular No. 61-2004 appropriating P80M (P40M each for CA Cebu and CA Cagayan de Oro) from the 20% equipment and facilities allocation of the Judiciary Development Fund; P40M for Cebu later increased to P70M in December 2005, prompting design changes; 'the provincial government of Cebu was generous enough to donate to the judiciary this more than 2,000 square meter piece of land'

Three-fold credit: 'it brings to fruition the efforts initiated by Chief Justice Davide, the commitment of the present leadership of the Supreme Court, and the generous support of the provincial government of Cebu'

Cebu historical parallel: April 14, 1521 -- advent of Christianity in the Philippines; King Humabon and Queen Juana received baptism in Cebu; 'in much the same way, we are once again making Cebu a gateway, this time to the judiciary. You can say that in 1521, Cebu helped spread the faith; in 2006, it facilitated access to justice.'

ACID connection: new CA building addresses the 'A' (Access to justice by the poor) in ACID; 'litigants will no longer have to bear the additional expense of flying to Manila to argue or follow up their appealed cases'
Values reminder: DHL for 26,000 court employees (dedication to duty, honesty in every way, full loyalty); four Ins for the nine CA justices (integrity, independence, industry, intelligence)

stances.claim: The CA Cebu building addresses the first and most fundamental ACID problem: limited access to justice by the poor. By eliminating the need for Visayan litigants to fly to Manila to follow up or argue appealed cases, the building translates the abstract constitutional mandate of equal access to justice into a concrete material reality.
stances.rhetorical_move: access-through-infrastructure argument: the physical building as the concrete translation of the constitutional access mandate
stances.confidence: asserted as the governing public service rationale

notable_anecdotes: The 1521-to-2006 Cebu parallel: 'On April 14, 1521, the advent of Christianity in these islands was ushered in by Cebu, when King Humabon and his wife, Queen Juana, received the sacrament of baptism. In much the same way, we are once again making Cebu a gateway, this time to the judiciary. In 1521, Cebu helped spread the faith; in 2006, it facilitated access to justice.' -- the most historically resonant local-to-national institutional metaphor in the corpus.

The Manila-flight burden eliminated: 'our litigants will no longer have to bear the additional expense of flying to Manila to argue or follow up their appealed cases' -- the most concrete, tangible benefit statement of any judicial infrastructure speech in the corpus.

Three-way credit: the building 'brings to fruition the efforts initiated by Chief Justice Davide, the commitment of the present leadership of the Supreme Court, and the generous support of the provincial government of Cebu' -- the three institutional actors whose cooperation produced the result.

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered November 24, 2006 in Cebu -- twelve days before CJP's mandatory retirement; greeted with 'Maayong hapon kaninyong tanan' -- this address by CJP marks the laying of the marker for the permanent CA Cebu building. The history: on December 4, 2004, CJ Davide issued Administrative Circular No. 61-2004, appropriating P40M (from the Judiciary Development Fund's 20% equipment allocation) for the CA Cebu building; this was later increased to P70M in December 2005; the provincial government of Cebu donated the more than 2,000 sqm site. Three-way credit: the dream was 'initiated by Chief Justice Davide, the commitment of the present leadership of the Supreme Court, and the generous support of the provincial government of Cebu.' The governing historical metaphor: 'On April 14, 1521, the advent of Christianity in these islands was ushered in by Cebu, when King Humabon and his wife, Queen Juana, received the sacrament of baptism. In much the same way, we are once again making Cebu a gateway, this time to the judiciary. In 1521, Cebu helped spread the faith; in 2006, it facilitated access to justice.' The ACID connection: the building addresses the 'A' (Access) -- 'litigants will no longer have to bear the additional expense of flying to Manila to argue or follow up their appealed cases.' Values reminder for the 26,000 court employees: DHL (dedication, honesty, loyalty); for the nine CA Cebu justices: four Ins (integrity, independence, industry, intelligence). Closes in Cebuano: 'Daghang salamat!'
